newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil still in doldrums, spreads unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil still in doldrums, spreads unchanged.

text.p: European gas oil differentials were stable in slow, holiday-affected discussion on Tuesday, with sellers having to work harder than buyers to drum up interest, traders said.
Outright prices firmed around $1 a tonne in line with September IPE futures, which were trading quietly at $170.50 at 1130 GMT in a narrow, 25-cent range.
A cargo of low sulphur EN590 diesel was rumoured sold to a British major early on Tuesday or late on Monday at around September +$4.75 cif NWE on a private and confidential basis.
Elsewhere the market appeared lifeless. German heating oil was September +$0.50/+$0.75 for September 1-10. Late August was September +$0.75 offered with no bid.
"Sellers are more interested than buyers," one trader said.
The barge market was equally slow.
"It's ridiculous. There's nothing," said a barge player. "Sellers are more aggressive. But if you want good volume of running refinery, you won't find it. It's not available."
Rotterdam refinery was at September IPE flat for August, with September at a premium of $1 to September IPE. EN590 was at premiums of +$4.75/$5.00 for storage at $5.50 for refinery.
